_sources.discrepancies: NCSL lists VA as 'non-photo ID requested'. SoS confirms voters may show a non-photo document (utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, government document with name and address) or a photo ID. Virginia implemented expanded no-excuse absentee voting (any registered voter may vote absentee). 2026-06-10 verification (elections.virginia.gov upcoming elections): MAJOR CHANGE — Virginia moved its 2026 primary from June to AUGUST 4, 2026 amid the redistricting push (the file previously had June 9, which was wrong even before the move; the statutory date was June 16). Primary: registration deadline July 24, 2026; early voting June 19-August 1 (offices closed June 19 for Juneteenth open June 18); mail-ballot application deadline July 24. General: registration deadline October 23, 2026 (file previously had Oct 13); early voting Sept 18-Oct 31 confirmed; mail-ballot application deadline Oct 23. Virginia offers same-day registration with a provisional ballot after the deadline through Election Day — sameDayRegistration corrected to true. Mail-ballot application deadline corrected from '5 days' to the official 11-days-before rule.

earlyVoting.notes: Virginia moved its 2026 primary to August 4. Early in-person voting runs Friday, June 19 through 5 p.m. Saturday, August 1, 2026 (offices closed June 19 for Juneteenth open Thursday, June 18). Voters may register after July 24 and vote with a provisional ballot through Election Day.
Early in-person voting runs Friday, September 18 through 5 p.m. Saturday, October 31, 2026. Voters may register after October 23 and vote with a provisional ballot through Election Day.
No-excuse in-person absentee voting available beginning 45 days before Election Day through the Saturday before. Contact your local registrar for locations and hours.

acceptedIds: Virginia driver's license or ID card
Any U.S. or Virginia government-issued photo ID
Student ID from a Virginia college or university (with photo)
Utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck, or other government document showing name and address
votingRules.expirationRule: Photo IDs used for voting should not be expired. Non-photo documents showing name and address are also acceptable, and voters without ID may sign an ID Confirmation Statement: https://www.elections.virginia.gov/casting-a-ballot/voter-id/
votingRules.impedimentDeclaration: If a voter cannot provide an acceptable form of ID, they may cast a provisional ballot and present acceptable ID to the general registrar by noon on the Friday after the election.
votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: Virginia does not prohibit phones in polling places. Voters may not photograph their ballot or otherwise interfere with other voters.
additionalRules: Open primary: Virginia voters do not register by party. Any voter may participate in any party's primary.
No legislative primary runoffs in Virginia.

eligibility: Any registered Virginia voter may request an absentee ballot without providing a reason
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: Must be received by the local registrar by 5 p.m. eleven days before the election (October 23, 2026 for the general election)
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by the registrar by 7 p.m. on Election Day, or postmarked by Election Day and received within 3 days after
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Must arrive by 7 p.m. Election Day, or be postmarked by Election Day and received within 3 days after.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: Virginia has an open primary with no party registration (Va. Code Ann. §24.2-530). Virginia does not register voters by party. Any registered voter may participate in any party's primary by requesting that party's ballot.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Virginia tiene una primaria abierta sin registro de partido (Va. Code Ann. §24.2-530). Virginia no registra a los votantes por partido. Cualquier votante registrado puede participar en la primaria de cualquier partido solicitando la boleta de ese partido.
